h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, ט׳ Ki Savo, 9
Prayer Renews the Heart Through the Humility of Bikkurim

p: In the Midrash (Tanchuma, beginning of this parshah)
and expounds what the verse says:
"Come, let us prostrate ourselves and bow,
נִבְרְכָה לִפְנֵי ה׳ עוֹשֵׂנוּ (תְּהִלִּים צה, ו)
let us kneel before Hashem our Maker" (Tehillim 95:6).
What then does it teach by saying
Rather, Moshe foresaw with ruach hakodesh
and saw that the Beis HaMikdash was destined to be destroyed
and the bikkurim destined to cease;
he arose and instituted for Yisrael
what connection does prayer have to bikkurim?
after the entire passage of bikkurim,
לִהְיוֹת לְךָ לֵאלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם כו, יז)
לִהְיוֹת לוֹ לְעַם סְגוּלָּה וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם כו, יח)
to be for Him a treasured people, etc." (ibid. 26:18).
that the essence of the act of bringing bikkurim
is to show that one nullifies himself
with all his powers to the Root.
And about this the expression is used,
וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתָ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ (שָׁם כו, י)
"and you shall prostrate yourself before Hashem your God" (ibid. 26:10);
for it is known that prostration
is with outstretched hands and feet
that is, one nullifies himself entirely
to Hashem, may He be blessed.
there also comes a renewal in the heart,
he becomes like a new creation,
with renewal in words of Torah.
And about this it says afterward,
as Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
בְּכָל יוֹם יִהְיוּ בְּעֵינֶיךָ חֲדָשִׁים וְכוּלֵּי
"Every day they should be new in your eyes, etc."
הַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם
that is, also each and every day,
And on this it brings the pasuk,
"Come, let us prostrate ourselves and bow, let us kneel, etc.";
also to the continuation of the verse,
and we are the people of His pasture, etc.;
הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקוֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ (שָׁם צה, ז)
today, if you will hearken to His voice" (ibid. 95:7)
the word "today" is used here too.
"Come, let us prostrate ourselves and bow,"
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן בִּיטּוּל לְהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ
which too is a matter of nullification to the Root,
to pour out one's soul before Hashem;
as they said in the Gemara (Berachos 34b):
That is, because in him there shone in his prayer
such a revelation of the Kingship of Heaven
that he came to the divesting of physicality.
And from this there also comes about
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז בְּפָסוּק זֶה גַּם כֵּן
And to this this pasuk alludes as well,
שֶׁזֶּה נִפְעָל גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה
that this too is brought about through prayer:
מְרַמֵּז עַל אֶת ה׳ הֶאֱמַרְתָּ הַיּוֹם
alludes to "You have affirmed Hashem today
"and we are the people of His pasture"
alludes to "and Hashem has affirmed you today
to be for Him a treasured people."
"Today, if you will hearken to His voice"
that is, the aspect of renewal
that is born in the heart

Prayer Returns Every Power to Its Root
